A railway of about 1,860 kilometres from the port of Dar es Salaam in Tanzania to Kapiri Mposhi in central Zambia, built from 1970 to 1975 by the People's Republic of China.

Zambia had no coast, and its copper from the Copperbelt went out by railways through white-ruled Rhodesia, Portuguese Angola and Mozambique, and South Africa. When Rhodesia declared independence under white rule in 1965, President Kenneth Kaunda and Julius Nyerere of Tanzania wanted a line that avoided them. The World Bank and Western governments refused to pay for it. China agreed, with an interest-free loan, as told in China builds TAZARA.

Tens of thousands of Tanzanian and Zambian workers and Chinese workers and engineers built it, through mountains and swamps, and it was finished ahead of schedule. It was China's largest aid project of the time. In later decades the line suffered from poor upkeep and lost traffic to roads, and it has been the subject of new Chinese investment plans.
sum: A railway of about 1,860 kilometres from the port of Dar es Salaam in Tanzania to Kapiri Mposhi in central Zambia, built from 1970 to 1975 by the People's Republic of China.
